precepts.text: For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves. Baruch clears up the word bethink easily. In the land of our captivity, the land of our enemy, we shall remember ourselves.
precepts.point: Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives, and repent, and make supplication unto thee in the land of them that carried them captives, saying, We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness. Bethink means to remember. What is Solomon saying here in prayer? Solomon saw in the spirit us being put on ships and scattered all over the world, yokes being put upon our necks, and then being destroyed afterwards so much that we would turn our own eyes against our own people and attack them. That is why he said they must bethink or remember themselves, because Solomon saw in the spirit that we were going to lose ourselves, lose our identity, and try to seek others or recreate ourselves, and not recreate ourselves in the image of God. And we can only say, we have sinned, if we know who we are.

note.label: Foundational Babylonian Advocates: Division Among the Dispersion

precepts.why:
Solomon prays, “Yet if they shall bethink themselves in the land whither they were carried captives”. Bethink is not a common word we use today. Baruch clears it up easily: “For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.”

“For I knew that they would not hear me”: that is why he put us in captivity, because we are a stiffnecked people. He delivered us to the enemy, by ships, “unto the land of the enemy, far or near”. This land is the land of our enemy: our enemy conquered us and made this land his land. Far is here, far from Jerusalem; near is Africa or Madagascar, colonised just the same.

“but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.” In our captivity, in the land of our enemy, we shall remember ourselves. That is what bethink means: remember, call to mind. Solomon saw in the spirit our people put on the ships and scattered all over the world, yokes put upon our necks, and destroyed so much that we would turn our own eyes against our own people and attack them. He saw that we would lose ourselves and our identity, and try to seek others or recreate ourselves, instead of in the image of God.

So first we must remember ourselves. We can only say “We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness” if we know who we are. And once you learn who you are, you learn who the enemy is by default. As long as you don’t know who you are, you will make your own people from the continent or the Caribbean your enemy, while the white man gets a pass.

precepts.why:
Baruch says, “Thus we were cast down, and not exalted, because we have sinned against the Lord our God”, and “unto us and to our fathers open shame, as appeareth this day.” Here in America we have open shame, because we departed from our God and refuse to come back and repent. Lamentations shows what that open shame looks like.

“All that pass by clap their hands at thee; they hiss and wag their head at the daughter of Jerusalem.” All the other nations pass by and clap their hands at us. They are happy we are thrown down, happy we are not exalted, happy we are at the bottom.

“Is this the city that men call The perfection of beauty, The joy of the whole earth?” Everybody knows we are the perfection of beauty: our skin, our hair, our lips, our eyes. Flip the coin and look at Esau, wrinkled and dried up with skin cancer, twenty years old looking forty. And we are the joy of the whole earth: even in the lowest state we are in, everything we do, everybody follows.

“All thine enemies have opened their mouth against thee: they hiss and gnash the teeth.” Starting with Edom on down. You go in the Chinese hair store, the nail shop, the gas station, the Arab store, the East Indian store, and they open their mouth against you; they don’t give a damn about you. “They say, We have swallowed her up: certainly this is the day that we looked for; we have found, we have seen it.” We don’t have a community, only neighborhoods, and in our own neighborhoods they own everything and we are the consumers. This is the day they hoped for, to see us break our laws and fall.

But now the Lord is waking his prophets back up to get his people back in order, to turn this place upside down, so we can have rulership on this earth again in righteousness.

precepts.text: Calling the blessing and the curse to mind is Israel remembering themselves in the land of their captivities.
precepts.point: And shalt return unto the Lord thy God, and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee, thou and thy children, with all thine heart and with all thy soul. The stipulation of returning is keeping the commandments; you cannot just say I accept the Lord in my heart. That does not work. And your children must be in order under your household too; they cannot fake it either.

note.label: Deuteronomy 30: Call the Curses to Mind and Choose Life

precepts.why:
With all that being said in the curses, here is the goodness of the Most High: he said, I am going to punish you, but he gave us the solution to get up out of the curses. “when all these things are come upon thee, the blessing and the curse, which I have set before thee, and thou shalt call them to mind among all the nations, whither the Lord thy God hath driven thee”. Baruch tells you what calling them to mind is: “For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves.”

The Most High knew we would not hear him, stiffnecked as we are, so the remembering happens in the land of our captivities. We are remembering ourselves now: we know we got here on ships, we know we did not speak the white man's language when he came to the west coast of Africa, we know we rise when the alarm clock goes off and work for food, water and drink, and we know Christianity is a slave religion forced on our ancestors. That is calling the curses to mind.

Then the stipulation: “And shalt return unto the Lord thy God, and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day, thou and thy children, with all thine heart, and with all thy soul”. Returning is keeping the commandments. You cannot just say I accept the Lord in my heart; that does not work. And your children must be in order under your household too; they cannot fake it either.

precepts.point: Baruch is told not to seek great things for himself, for the Most High will bring evil upon all flesh, but his life He will give him for a prey in all places wherever he goes.

note.label: Jeremiah 45: The Word of Comfort to Baruch the Scribe

precepts.why:
The Most High speaks directly, “unto thee, O Baruch”, and the words of the scribe Baruch are preserved in the Apocrypha, so get yourself a 1611 King James Version Bible with the Apocrypha. There Baruch records what our forefathers learned through the prophets: “If ye will not hear my voice, surely this very great multitude shall be turned into a small number among the nations, where I will scatter them.”

“For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people: but in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves. And shall know that I am the Lord their God: for I will give them an heart, and ears to hear: And they shall praise me in the land of their captivity, and think upon my name, And return from their stiff neck, and from their wicked deeds: for they shall remember the way of their fathers, which sinned before the Lord.”

This is the understanding the christian church lacks. In the land of our captivity we would remember ourselves, know that he is the Lord our God, and return from our stiff neck and our wicked deeds. One way we think upon his name is rehearsing his righteous acts at the Passover. The Lord broke down what he built and plucked up what he planted, even the whole land, but the scattering was never the end of the story for this stiffnecked people.
